newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS to lose Greenland monopoly.
newsitem.headline: SAS to lose Greenland monopoly.

text.p: Denmark and its North Atlantic territory of Greenland agreed on Thursday to end a Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) monopoly on scheduled flights between the two.

A joint statement from the Danish transport ministry and the Greenland home-rule government said that the two sides agreed that freight and post traffic should be completely deregulated, while SAS should have at least one competitor for its passenger traffic.
"This is a great gain for Greenland's people, business life and tourism," its transport minister Peter Samuelsen said.

Charter aircraft have recently made occasional freight runs under special license but SAS has a sole concession for scheduled traffic on the 3,400 Km (2,100 mile) transatlantic route between Copenhagen and Greenland's Kangerlussuaq airport.
Thursday's agreement did not say if changes would be introduced before the official expiry of the SAS concession in the year 2005.
The Danish, Swedish and Norwegian governments own SAS jointly with private investors.
